text.p: Latvian fish cannery Kaija plans a 20 percent increase in profits in 1997 and that sales volume would be 14.45 million lats, chairman Arno Karklinsh told Reuters on Thursday.
He did not give a figure for 1996 profits as he said they were not yet available.
He also said that sales in January and February were "significantly higher" than sales in the same months in 1996.
Karklinsh also said that production in January and February was 2,110 tonnes of product of which it sold 1,715 tonnes.
Production figures for January and February in 1996 were 1,871 tonnes of which it sold 1,473 tonnes.
"In 1997 we plan to introduce more than 20 new types of produce, including culinary products," Karklinsh said.
Kaija is the largest ocean fish producer in the Baltic states, with some 70 percent of raw material being ocean catch.
The main markets are still Russia and the CIS although more attention is to be devoted to the Baltics, especially Lithuania.
